sources.entry: Pattern Recognition and Machine Learning by Christopher M. Bishop

summary.name: Pattern Recognition and Machine Learning
summary.one_liner: A 2006 Springer textbook by Christopher M. Bishop that gives a comprehensive introduction to pattern recognition and machine learning from a Bayesian and graphical-models perspective.
use_cases: learning machine learning from a textbook
reference for probabilistic and graphical models
summary.what_it_does: The book presents pattern recognition and machine learning as two facets of one field, covering Bayesian methods, graphical models for describing probability distributions, and approximate inference algorithms such as variational Bayes and expectation propagation. It also covers kernel-based models. It includes a self-contained introduction to basic probability theory and assumes multivariate calculus and linear algebra. Reviews note about 700 pages and more than 400 exercises, with supporting material for instructors on the publisher's site.
notable: Presents the Bayesian viewpoint and uses graphical models to describe probability distributions
Covers approximate inference such as variational Bayes and expectation propagation
Includes around 400 exercises and instructor material
caveats: Requires multivariate calculus and linear algebra background
Accessibility information for the book was listed as coming soon
Published in 2006; the page describes developments from roughly the prior decade
